title: Unraveling hepatotoxicity: mechanistic insights into food chain-transferred nanoplastics disrupting PPAR signaling and liver metabolism.
authors: Shi, Yutian; Qu, Xiaochuan; Han, Yuewen; Li, Yuheng; Sun, Guoming; Sun, Huayang; Lu, Chang; Qu, Ruixuan; Zhang, Meng; Zhang, Ning; Zhao, Xin; Liu, Baoqin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学与分子对接/动力学模拟研究纳米塑料与PPAR配体结合域的互作及其肝毒性机制，虽涉及蛋白-配体结合建模，但对象为小分子-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法可迁移性有限，仅部分相关。
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing global plastic consumption, nanoplastics (NPs) formed from the degradation of plastic waste have become widespread in ecological media. These particles can transfer through the food chain to higher trophic organisms, accumulating in organs and posing a health risk. As the primary metabolic organ for ingested NPs, the liver demands urgent investigation into the toxicity mechanisms induced by these particles. Here, we employed a multi-omics-integrated approach to investigate the impact of food chain-transferred nanoplastics (FCT-NPs) on hepatic metabolic and detoxification functions in mice. Our findings demonstrated substantial enrichment of FCT-NPs in liver, resulting in histopathological damage, impaired liver function, and metabolic homeostasis disruption. Transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses collectively identified the suppression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling pathway as a central mechanism of FCT-NPs-induced hepatotoxicity. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed a potential direct interaction site between NPs and the PPAR ligand-binding domain, suggesting a mechanistic basis for toxicity. Specifically, inhibition of the PPAR pathway downregulated key downstream processes, disrupting fatty acid transport and metabolism, retinoid and steroid metabolism, and redox balance. This study provides the first mechanistic evidence linking dietary FCT-NPs exposure to PPAR interaction and metabolic dysfunction, thereby advancing risk assessment for NPs-induced liver injury in both mammals and humans.
abstract_zh: 在全球塑料消费量不断增长的背景下，由塑料废弃物降解形成的纳米塑料（nanoplastics, NPs）已在生态介质中广泛分布。这些颗粒可通过食物链传递至更高营养级生物，在器官中积累并对健康构成风险。作为摄入NPs的主要代谢器官，肝脏亟需研究这些颗粒诱导的毒性机制。本研究采用多组学整合方法，探讨经食物链传递的纳米塑料（food chain-transferred nanoplastics, FCT-NPs）对小鼠肝脏代谢和解毒功能的影响。结果表明，FCT-NPs在肝脏中显著富集，导致组织病理学损伤、肝功能受损及代谢稳态紊乱。转录组学、蛋白质组学和代谢组学分析共同揭示，过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor, PPAR）信号通路的抑制是FCT-NPs诱导肝毒性的核心机制。分子对接和动力学模拟揭示了NPs与PPAR配体结合域之间潜在的直接相互作用位点，为毒性机制提供了基础。具体而言，PPAR通路的抑制下调了关键下游过程，扰乱脂肪酸转运与代谢、视黄醇和类固醇代谢以及氧化还原平衡。本研究首次提供了将膳食FCT-NPs暴露与PPAR相互作用及代谢功能障碍联系起来的机制证据，从而推进了对NPs诱导哺乳动物及人类肝损伤的风险评估。
